translation_updates.summary: Daniel Kahneman (1934–2024) was an Israeli-American psychologist widely regarded as a founder of behavioral economics and best known for his work on the psychology of judgment and decision-making, for which he was awarded the 2002 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences together with Vernon L. Smith. Working with Amos Tversky and others, he established a cognitive basis for common human errors arising from heuristics and biases and developed prospect theory, findings that challenged the assumption of human rationality in modern economic theory. His 2011 book Thinking, Fast and Slow summarized much of this research and became a best seller.

An Investigation of the Laws of Thought is a book by the English mathematician George Boole, published in 1854. It developed an algebraic treatment of logic in which logical reasoning is expressed through symbolic operations, laying the groundwork for what is now known as Boolean algebra. It is a founding work of modern symbolic and mathematical logic.
